title: fix(spec): the flows translation group goes live — the flow runner reads flows.FLOW.label
body:
Fixes #20318
Clause-②: no

Stage 3 of the card: the objectstack half that follows objectui's new reader. Three things land together. The `flows` translation group goes `live` in the liveness ledger, in both halves. The tests that pinned the old ledger state move with it. And the CLI's coverage walker demands a flow's own label only where the runner can show it, per `domain:cli`'s ruling A on #6024. Every check measured here is green, `check:i18n-coverage` included, and every example sits at its committed baseline.

## The reader, measured at the pin

`.objectui-sha` on `main` is `0abd4f9f8769`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 39a3e91fad 0abd4f9f8769` exits 0, so the pin carries objectui PR 11636. A positive answer proves itself even on a shallow clone. Read at `0abd4f9f8769`, read-only:

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/FlowRunner.tsx:268-275` `displayFlowLabel` returns `translateFlow({ name: flowName, label: flowLabel }, bundle, { locale: language }).label || flowName`. That is the active language's `flows.FLOW.label`, then the served `flowLabel`, then the API name.
- `:377` computes `shownFlowLabel`. `:541` draws it in the dialog header, above the step's `DialogTitle`.
- `:441` hands `displayFlowLabel(...)` to the `flowRunner.completed` completion toast. The toast shows only when the flow authored no `successMessage`.
- `:211-229` `activeFlowsBundle` reads the active language's `flows` group from the i18next `translation` resource tree. The `screens` overlay uses the same read.
- `translateFlow` is imported from `@objectstack/spec/system` (`:163`).
- The served label comes from `packages/app-shell/src/utils/flowResponse.ts:234-235` (`servedFlowLabel`, on the trigger and resume 200 bodies).
- The three hosts open the runner with that label: `hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:653`, `views/RecordDetailView.tsx:1118`, and `apps/console/src/pages/developer/FlowRunsPage.tsx:310`.
- The reader grep from `domain:cli`'s ruling was re-run at the pin. `git grep -E "translateFlow\b|displayFlowLabel"` over `packages/`, excluding tests and stories, still returns 8 hits: 7 in `FlowRunner.tsx` and 1 comment in `metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-nested-selection.ts`. No reader of a non-screen flow's translated label exists, and the pin has not moved.

## What changed

- **`packages/spec/liveness/translation.json`**
  - `flows.children.label`: `planned` to `live`, with `verifiedAt 2026-10-05` and `evidenceScope: cross-repo`. The evidence uses `file#symbol` anchors, with each objectui pointer prefixed `objectui @0abd4f9f8:` as the ledger README prescribes. The `producer` names the engine's `AutomationResult.flowLabel` copy, the objectui lift and hosts, and the bundle delivery chain the `screens` row already cites.
  - The `flows` container: both children are now `live`, so it is `live` too, with its own evidence. It drops `authorWarn` and `authorHint`, because a `live` row refuses them.
  - The `screens` row's note gains one dated line saying that its "NOT flipped with it" clause is superseded.
- **`packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/translation.md`**: regenerated with `gen:liveness-counts`. `translation` is now `26 live · 0 planned`, up from `25 · 1`.
- **`content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`**: the boundary bullet now says what is true.
  - Both halves are applied: `screens` through the screen copy, and `label` through the runner header and the toast.
  - Three strings stay outside the group: the screen `description`, an authored `successMessage`, and the runner chrome.
  - The tooling asks for the keys, and asks for a flow's own `label` only when the flow has a screen node.
  - The "the day the runner lands" sentence is gone.
- **`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`**: the `flows` TSDoc said "The flow's own `label` is read by nothing yet". It now names the reader and the pin. This is the JSDoc only. No `.describe()` string moved, so nothing generated was built from it.
- **`examples/`**: the three screen wizards get their `flows` copy in every supported locale. That covers `crm_convert_lead_wizard` (zh-CN, 4 strings), `showcase_reassign_wizard` (zh-CN, 3) and `quick_add_task` (zh-CN and ja-JP, 7 each).
- **Changesets**, measured with `npm pack --dry-run`:
  - `.changeset/20318-flows-translation-live.md` is an `@objectstack/spec` patch. `liveness/translation.json`, `liveness/state-counts/translation.md` and `src/system/translation.zod.ts` all ship, and the control `dist/index.js` ships too.
  - `.changeset/20318-cli-flow-label-demand.md` is an `@objectstack/cli` patch. `dist/utils/i18n-extract.js` ships (597 files packed; the control `package.json` is present), and the built file carries the predicate.
  - `content/docs` and `examples/` publish nothing.

### The flow label is demanded only for a flow the runner can open (`domain:cli` ruling A)

- **`packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts`**: one predicate in `walkScreenFlows`. The `flows.FLOW.label` entry is emitted only when `collectFlowNodesDeep`, the node universe the screens walk already reads at any depth, yields a `screen` node. Nothing else in the walker moves: the node list is computed one statement earlier, so the label entry keeps its place ahead of the screen entries.
  - The predicate's comment names `FlowRunner` as the reader it mirrors (ruling condition (b)). It also says the predicate widens in the same change as any future reader of a non-screen flow's label.
- **Pins** in `packages/cli/test/i18n-flow-screen-coverage.test.ts` (ruling condition (a)):
  - a scheduled flow with a region and no screen node emits no `flows.FLOW.label` entry;
  - a flow whose only screen node sits two regions deep (a loop body, then a parallel branch) still emits it;
  - in one tree holding both flows, the coverage gate asks for the screen flow's label and not the other's.
  - The existing "reads the region TABLE" test now expects `[]` for its flow, whose only screen-shaped object sits in an `http` payload, so the flow has no screen node and owes no label. It gains a lit control: the same flow with one real screen emits the label and that screen, and still not the payload object.
- **Control legs**, each run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` and proved by "ok mutation landed" and "ok restored: blob == HEAD (521163a07d87) and `git diff HEAD` is empty". The test imports `../src`, so no build is in the path.
  - **The predicate removed** (the label pushed unconditionally) reads `Tests 3 failed | 21 passed (24)`: the no-screen pin, the one-tree pin and the region-table test.
  - **The predicate over the flat top-level `flow.nodes`** instead of the deep universe reads `Tests 2 failed | 22 passed (24)`: the region-nested pin and the one-tree pin. The region-nested pin cannot go red by removing the predicate, since an unconditional label satisfies it, so this second leg is the one that proves it.

### The tests that pinned the old ledger move with the flip

These are test and comment edits, with cross-lane declarations to `domain:cli` and `domain:devx`. No pin was deleted.

- **`packages/cli/test/i18n-flow-liveness-gate.test.ts`**: its real-ledger pins now read the post-flip ledger.
  - The census pin: `authorWarnedTranslationGroups()` equals `[]`, still an equality.
  - Its "can say no" twin gets its positive from the same reader, `authorWarnedProperties('object')` naming `externalSharingModel`.
  - The walk with the ledger's own set equals the ungated walk, and `flows` is among its roots.
  - The untranslated wizard draws exactly five `i18n/missing-flow` keys, and the translated one draws none.
  - The collision pin: omitting the keys draws demand and no warning, and authoring them draws neither. A witness in the same call raises the one warned object row.
  - The skeleton scaffolds `flows`.
  - The injected-set pin "gates whatever the ledger names" still holds the gate for a warned group.
- **`packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.test.ts`**:
  - The locale-keyed walk pins and the runtime-`TranslationItem` anti-fixture now read a planted synthetic `planned` + `authorWarn` group row. They go through `lintLivenessPropertiesFromLedgerDir`, the seam the synthetic `field` ledger already uses.
  - The real-ledger `translation.flows (planned)` case splits into a silence pin on the shipped row (beside a witness that still warns) and a planted twin that holds the planned-with-`authorHint` wording.
  - The two silence pins now author `flows` too.
  - The `authorWarnedProperties` census reads `[]` for translation, with the `object` positive.
  - The anti-drift pin asks over every top-level row the translation ledger governs, and over the `object` type's non-empty warned set.
- **Comments only**:
  - In `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts`, the extract-surface header lists `inlineHelpText` and says why `flows` is walked, and the `authorWarnedTranslationGroups` docblock says the set is empty today.
  - The header of `packages/cli/test/i18n-flow-screen-coverage.test.ts`.
  - `translateFlow`'s docblock in `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`.

No new id: no new or rewritten test title, test string, comment headline or runtime string carries a tracker id as its citation. The new pins, the predicate's comment and the CLI changeset sentence cite behaviour and the reader, not a tracker number.

## What dropping `authorWarn` switched on, and what the predicate takes back

With the ledger flipped and no predicate, `os lint ... --json` reported 56 new `i18n/missing-flow` findings across the examples:

| example | findings | from screen flows | `label` of a flow with no screen node |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `app-crm` | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| `app-showcase` | 32 | 3 | 29 |
| `app-todo` (zh-CN + ja-JP) | 20 | 14 | 6 |

The 21 screen-flow strings are translated in this PR. The 35 label demands for flows that never open the runner are what the predicate removes. `check:i18n-coverage` now reads "OK (13 config(s), 621 baselined untranslated string(s), none new)". The ratchet is two-sided, so crm, showcase and todo sit exactly at their committed 101, 414 and 106. `scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json` is untouched, and none of the 35 inert strings is authored. `check:i18n` stays green.

## Tests and gates (at `bac6651dd7`, every package built with declarations)

- The build was `turbo run build --filter=!@objectstack/docs` (72 tasks, exit 0).
- CLI unit tier: `Test Files 259 passed (259)`, `Tests 3786 passed (3786)`. That is 3783 plus the three new predicate pins. The packed-`.d.ts` pins are included.
- Full `@objectstack/lint` suite: `Tests 5629 passed (5629)`.
- `@objectstack/cli` typecheck exit 0, test layer included ("held in test-typecheck-debt.json", unchanged).
- The re-pinned files: the CLI screen-coverage file reads `Tests 24 passed (24)` at HEAD. lint `lint-liveness-properties` is unchanged since `dfa18e7699`, where it read `Tests 97 passed (97)`, and it is inside the 5629 above. The flip's control leg on the re-pinned real-ledger pins (pre-flip ledger restored by a trap, proved by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`) read CLI `6 failed | 23 passed` and lint `5 failed | 92 passed`, while the planted pins stayed green.
- `check:liveness` exit 0. `check:i18n-coverage` exit 0, as above.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 115. The `--ran` reconciliation reads "115 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 115 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED", and all 115 exited 0.
- `origin/main` (`9f9510f25e`) touches none of these 15 files and does not move `.objectui-sha` (still `0abd4f9f8769`; its last change is `8832655af2`). Not merged, not rebased. The one derived-from file main changed, `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, gained an objectql test pin unrelated to this diff.

## Acceptance notes

- The flip, the re-pins and the predicate are one commit set on purpose. Each re-pinned file pins the real ledger state, and the predicate is what lets the flip's demand side match its reader, so any part landed alone is red.
- Ruling condition (c) is still live until this lands: if `.objectui-sha` moves first, re-run the reader grep on the new pin, and stop if a reader of a non-screen flow's translated label has appeared.
